application_guidance.input_pattern: A common quantitative factorial-power derivative envelope and a fresh select-one-gradient oracle with fixed all-execution sample budget.
read_original_when: Instantiating or modifying the lower construction, oracle information or dimension dependence.
Changing quantitative derivative normalization or any baseline budget.
sensitive_conditions: C-infinity or entire dependence alone does not imply a uniform improvement; Appendix G.3 retains Theta(epsilon^-6) without a common quantitative envelope.
Do not let p grow inside constants from the arbitrary fixed-list corollary.
Do not substitute expected stopping cost, squared-norm accuracy, paired-gradient charging or sample reuse.
Strict L_1>mu is part of this theorem; the boundary case is separate.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Uniform worst-instance expected norm with a deterministic sample cap on every execution; no universal success-probability convention is imposed.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Depend only on fixed baseline budgets and M,Lambda_s,beta, independent of p and dimension for the envelope theorem. Arbitrary finite-list corollary constants and threshold may depend on that list and fixed p.
complexity_scope.oracle: Fresh globally unbiased select-one full population-gradient samples with conditional variance at most sigma^2; every sample charged; no sample reuse or higher-order feedback.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: An arbitrary upper-variable output xhat; target is E||grad Phi(xhat)||<=epsilon, not expected squared norm.
complexity_scope.regime: Nondegenerate baseline L_1>mu; fixed quantitative envelope independent of accuracy and order; dimensions may grow with accuracy.
complexity_scope.resource: Total raw f- and g-gradient samples, including every batch and rounding overhead. Computation and memory are unrestricted.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Upper witness is the Appendix B ordinary inner solve, projected stochastic adjoint using Appendix A differences, and normalized outer descent. Lower coverage is unrestricted adaptive randomized algorithms, including arbitrary output points.

evidence.statement_check: Complete Section 2 and Theorem 3.1/Corollaries 3.2–3.3 statements checked against original pp.5–7; selected long proof maps read through Appendices A–G.

content.intended_use: Identify the precise order–accuracy tradeoff for expected hypergradient norm under globally unbiased fresh first-order samples.

proofs.locator: Appendices A–B, equations (27)–(46) and final accounting on p.20
map: Appendix A.1 proves exact Chebyshev differentiation and W=n/h. A.2 uses the top Lipschitz Taylor remainder and factorial bounds to obtain bias<=a and W<=C_beta*r^beta*a^(-1/r). A.3 allocates independent node batches with variance<=sigma^2 W^2/B and cost<=B+n+1.

B.1 establishes hypergradient stability. B.2 supplies geometric batch allocation for a contraction. B.3 applies it to the ordinary lower solve; B.4 applies it to a projected adjoint with bounded additive differencing bias, without assuming that biased mean map is linear or conservative.

B.5 builds an independent outer direction with conditional expected error<=epsilon/8. Normalized descent with eta=epsilon/(2L_Phi), K=ceil(4Delta/(eta*epsilon)) and independently uniform I in {0,...,K-1} gives E||grad Phi(x_I)||<=3epsilon/4.

Choose a finite r minimizing r^beta epsilon^(-1/r) when beta>0; for beta=0 take r=min(p,ceil(log(1/epsilon))). Then W<=C D and n=O_beta(log(1/epsilon)). Summing charged direction costs gives N<=C epsilon^-4(1+W^2)+C epsilon^-2 log^2(1/epsilon)<=C epsilon^-4 D^2.
proofs.omitted_details: Long source proof is mapped rather than independently reproved. Stability and contraction interfaces are explicitly imported from B.1–B.4.
proofs.reading_coverage: Read Appendix A and B through the final p.20 sample accounting; native images pp.16–20 checked the displayed formulas.

map: C constructs extensive A_T and bounded frontier B_T from fixed smooth gates. Lemmas C.1–C.2 provide dimension-free frontier bounds, a descent barrier and the prefix-dependence interface. D wraps by a bounded-radius map plus a quadratic, retaining a nonstationarity barrier against arbitrary query norms.

E chooses h=K_0/D_{p,beta}(s), tau=K_0^(-3/2), lambda=s/tau, A=s^2/tau, T=floor(Delta*tau/(2C_Delta*s^2)). The scalar sine lift is f=A*A_U(x/lambda)+b*y and g=m*y^2/2-(m*A*h/b)*B_U(x/lambda)*sin(y/h), m=(mu+L_1)/2. E.2 controls the actual nonlinear lower root and hypergradient, rather than replacing them by an ideal linear root.

E.3 checks every population budget with one K_0 and an accuracy threshold uniform in p. F.1 separates the full lower signal v_U from (0,m*y), bounds ||v_U||<=C_*s*h globally, and uses a fresh Bernoulli(q_s) multiplier with q_s=C_*^2*s^2*h^2/sigma^2. This is the gradient of one of two fixed losses; f gradients are exact.

F.3 uses a deferred-prefix simulation, spherical-cap control and a union bound including the final output. For N*q_s<=T/8 and sufficiently large d, with probability at least 3/4 an unseen coordinate remains. The actual gradient barrier gives E||grad Phi||>=3s/16; averaging fixes a hard frame for each algorithm.
F.4 sets s=16epsilon and compares D(a*epsilon) to D(epsilon), yielding the claimed sample lower bound and d_x=O(epsilon^-2 log(1/epsilon)).
proofs.omitted_details: Imports the source's split-chain, wrapping and admissibility interfaces; no independent reconstruction or reproof of the full Hard Family is claimed.
proofs.reading_coverage: Read original-PDF Appendices C–F, printed pp.20–28, including construction formulas and information-to-error and budget calibration portions.

proofs.full_local_argument: For fixed p>=2 put M_-=min_{3<=j<=p+1}L_j>0 and M_+=max_{3<=j<=p+1}L_j. Keep all baseline budgets, including L_2, fixed. The beta=0, Lambda_s=1 envelope with M_- has every additional derivative budget no larger than the list; the envelope with M_+ has each no smaller. Thus F_- subset F_list subset F_+, with identical oracle and initialization contracts, including the common q=1 f bound L_2. Minimax monotonicity gives Q_-<=Q_list<=Q_+. Theorem 3.1 gives both outer rates Theta(epsilon^(-4-2/p)), since D_{p,0}=epsilon^(-1/p). Constants may depend on M_-,M_+ and hence the fixed list and p. For p=1 there is no additional list and Theorem 3.1 applies directly. The lower instances already have exact f gradients; the same upper procedure can consume exact f responses, so the sandwich also applies with exact f gradients. This is a local derivation conditional on the imported source Theorem 3.1, not a local reproof of that theorem.
map: Sandwich the fixed derivative list between two constant envelopes and apply the source Theorem 3.1.
proofs.omitted_details: Theorem 3.1 is the source-linked interface established by upper_map and lower_map in this record.
proofs.reading_coverage: Read Corollary 3.2 and complete G.1 class-inclusion argument.

assumptions: Fixed mu,L_0,L_2,Delta,sigma>0, L_1>mu and R_0>=0. Globally g(x,.) is mu-strongly convex; f(x,.) is L_0-Lipschitz; both full population gradients are jointly L_1-Lipschitz; g_xy and g_yy exist and are jointly L_2-Lipschitz.
At the supplied starting pair, Phi(x_0)-inf Phi<=Delta and ||y_0-y*(x_0)||<=R_0.

The displayed lower-variable derivatives exist and satisfy their global budgets. Lipschitz highest derivatives are interpreted through finite C^{k,1} Taylor remainders; an additional continuous derivative is not required. For q=1, the f bound uses the separately fixed L_2.
M,Lambda_s>0 and beta>=0 are fixed independently of order and accuracy. A qualitative C-infinity or analyticity assumption alone does not supply this envelope.

At each adaptive query (x,y), a call selects a in {f,g} and returns one full gradient sample G_a, conditionally on the past and query satisfying E G_a=grad a(x,y) and E||G_a-grad a(x,y)||^2<=sigma^2 over the entire domain. Independent fresh copies are available and every sample is evaluated only once and charged. Receiving both gradients costs two calls.
No function values, Hessians, HVPs, exact lower solutions or exact hypergradients are supplied by the base oracle. Samplewise uniform smoothness or convexity is not assumed.
statement.conclusion: c*epsilon^-4*D_{p,beta}(epsilon)^2 <= Q*_{p,beta}(epsilon) <= C*epsilon^-4*D_{p,beta}(epsilon)^2. The lower construction needs d_x=O(epsilon^-2 log(1/epsilon)) with constant independent of p. For every fixed finite p and arbitrary fixed positive list L_3,...,L_{p+1}, Q*_p(epsilon;list)=Theta_p(epsilon^(-4-2/p)), with list-dependent constants and threshold, also when all f gradients are exact. For beta>0 and t=log(1/epsilon), uniformly in p, Q*=Theta_beta(p^{2 beta}epsilon^(-4-2/p)) if p<=t/beta, and Theta_beta(epsilon^-4 t^{2 beta}) if p>=t/beta. For beta=0 the finite-p rate epsilon^(-4-2/p) is uniform in p and Q*_{infinity,0}=Theta(epsilon^-4); Q*_{infinity,1}=Theta(epsilon^-4 log^2(1/epsilon)). All lower bounds retain exact upper gradients.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Functions f,g are defined globally on R^{d_x} x R^{d_y}; y*(x)=argmin_y g(x,y), Phi(x)=f(x,y*(x)). Norms are Euclidean and induced operator norms. g_xy=D_y grad_x g and g_yy=D_y grad_y g. Lip_y is uniform over x. For p in N union {infinity}, impose Lip_y(D_y^q grad f)<=L_{q+1} and Lip_y(D_y^{q+1} grad g)<=L_{q+2}, 1<=q<=p-1; all positive q are included if p=infinity. The list is empty at p=1. L_2 is separately fixed, while L_j=M*Lambda_s^j*(j!)^beta for j>=3. Define D_{p,beta}(epsilon)=inf_{r in N,1<=r<=p} r^beta*epsilon^(-1/r), dropping the upper bound for infinite p. Q* is the least integer N permitting an algorithm informed of budgets, order and dimensions to use at most N samples on every execution and achieve sup over dimensions, admissible functions and admissible oracles E||grad Phi(xhat)||<=epsilon.
statement.parameter_domains: All finite dimensions in the minimax supremum; p positive integer or infinity; epsilon sufficiently small. Constants and the accuracy threshold are independent of p and dimension. Fixed finite-list corollary constants may depend on p and the list.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: There exist c,C,epsilon_0>0 depending only on the fixed baseline budgets and M,Lambda_s,beta such that simultaneously for every p in N union {infinity} and 0<epsilon<epsilon_0 the two-sided bound holds. The minimax lower bound covers unrestricted adaptive randomized algorithms, unrestricted computation, memory and output points, and arbitrary growing finite dimensions. Expectation is over algorithm and oracle randomness on each instance. The sample cap holds on every execution. The lower bound already holds with d_y=1, exact f gradients, zero initial inner error and a globally unbiased g oracle sampling gradients of two losses fixed before execution.
